title: Same grape, different places
subtitle: How climate changes the wine
objectives: Explain how climate changes a grape's flavour
Compare cool and warm climate versions of one grape
Predict style from a grape and a place

steps.title: Cool and warm
steps.body: Climate is the long-term pattern of a place. In a cool climate, grapes ripen slowly, keeping high acidity and giving lighter body and fresher, sometimes green, fruit. In a warm climate, grapes ripen fully, with more sugar, lower acidity and flavours of ripe or even jammy fruit.
steps.highlight: Cool: fresh, tart. Warm: ripe, full.

steps.title: Why acidity falls in heat
steps.body: As grapes ripen, sugar rises and acidity falls. Heat speeds both up, and warm nights let the vine burn off malic acid, one of the grape's main acids. That's why a Chardonnay from Chablis may have 12% alcohol and sharp acidity, while one from a hot valley might reach 14.5% with soft acidity and tropical fruit.
steps.highlight: Heat raises sugar and burns off acid

steps.prompt: A Chardonnay is lean, with green apple and 12% alcohol. Where does it most likely come from?
steps.explanation: Green apple, high acidity and moderate alcohol are signs of slow ripening in a cool place. A hot valley would give riper fruit and more alcohol.

steps.title: The grape and the place together
steps.body: Read a label as two clues. The grape tells you the basic character: aromas, skin, tannin. The place tells you how ripe it got. Sauvignon Blanc from the cool Loire tastes of grass and citrus; from warmer parts of Chile it leans towards passion fruit and melon. Same grape, different sun.
steps.highlight: Grape gives character; place gives ripeness

steps.prompt: Which are signs of a warm-climate wine?
steps.explanation: Heat gives more sugar, so more alcohol and riper fruit, and it lowers acidity. Sharp acidity is a cool-climate sign.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cool climates give fresher, lighter wines; warm ones riper and fuller
Heat raises sugar and lowers acidity
Grape gives the character, place gives the ripeness
